title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
oneLinerQuestion: Find the maximum depth or path height from the root to the farthest leaf node.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Maximum Depth of Binary Tree problem requires determining the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. This structure exhibits optimal substructure suited for Depth-First Search (DFS) recursion: the maximum depth of any subtree rooted at a given node is directly determined by taking 1 (accounting for the node itself) plus the greater of the maximum depths of its left and right subtrees.

- Step 1: Base Case (Null Nodes) — When traversing, if `root === null`, an empty subtree contributes zero depth. We immediately return 0.

- Step 2: Left Subtree Exploration — We recursively calculate the depth of the left branch: `const leftDepth = maxDepth(root.left)`.

- Step 3: Right Subtree Exploration — We recursively calculate the depth of the right branch: `const rightDepth = maxDepth(root.right)`.

- Step 4: Bottom-Up Depth Aggregation — We take the maximum of both subtree depths and add 1 for the current node: `return 1 + Math.max(leftDepth, rightDepth)`. As the recursion unwinds from the leaves back to the root, each level bubbles up its longest path.

- Step 5: Termination & Final Return — Once the root frame finishes resolving, the returned integer represents the overall maximum depth of the entire binary tree.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the total number of nodes, as every node in the binary tree is visited exactly once. Space Complexity: O(H) auxiliary space on the call stack, where H is the height of the tree (O(log N) for balanced trees, O(N) in the worst-case skewed tree).
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION maxDepth(root):
    IF root IS NULL THEN RETURN 0
    RETURN 1 + MAX(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right))
END FUNCTION
